key_insight: Electron beam curing of a rosin–castor-oil bio-based coating, especially F2 (MRGE/MCOA = 3:1), delivered the best overall balance of conversion, mechanical integrity, corrosion resistance, and dielectric performance.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a fast, renewable coating route for large electrical equipment such as thermal power generators, where protective insulation must withstand corrosion, salt exposure, and electrical stress.
method: Compared four MRGE/MCOA formulations under ultraviolet and electron-beam curing routes.
Evaluated surface C=C conversion, thermal behavior, morphology, mechanics, salt-spray corrosion, electrochemical barrier behavior, and AC dielectric breakdown strength.
Compared short-term immersion and long-term salt-spray damage evolution across curing conditions.
evidence_signal: F2-EB achieved 92±2% surface C=C conversion, Tg of 88±1 °C, 9H hardness, 5B adhesion, 10/10 salt-spray rating after 500 h, and 21.5±0.3 kV mm−1 dielectric breakdown strength.
watch_item: The study infers stronger network formation from performance trends, but through-thickness conversion and crosslink density were not directly measured.
paper_title: Electron Beam-Cured Rosin–Castor Oil Bio-Based Coatings for Large Thermal Power Generators
